original_question: What information about the dynamics or geometry of a billiard can be recovered from escape measurements alone, and to what extent can such measurements reveal the shape of the underlying domain?
target_in_paper: Section 11.6, Problem 11.19 (Inverse problems): What information can be extracted about the dynamics of a billiard from escape measurements? Can you “peep” the shape of a drum?
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies that the problem is an inverse problem based on escape data, that the goal is to recover information about billiard dynamics, and that the geometric aspect is specifically about whether the domain’s shape can be inferred from such data. It also keeps the paper’s cautious spirit by asking what can be recovered, rather than assuming complete reconstruction.
missing_details: The draft does not specify what the paper means by escape data: in the setup of Section 11.3, this is expressed through the survival probability P(t)=mu_0(Omega_t), where Omega_t is the set of phase points that have not yet hit the hole by time t.
It does not explicitly place the question in the setting of an open billiard, i.e. a billiard with one or more holes H through which trajectories escape.
It does not mention the role of the initial measure mu_0, which is part of the definition of the survival probability and hence part of what is being measured.
It does not name the billiard domain D whose geometry is under investigation.
It does not state that, in the paper’s surrounding context, escape observables also include the long-time escape rate gamma when that limit exists.

It slightly over-suggests full shape recovery; the paper’s formulation is deliberately weaker, asking what information can be extracted and whether one can 'peep' the shape at all, without asserting uniqueness or complete reconstruction.
refined_question: For an open billiard with hole(s) H and escape data given by the survival probabilities P(t)=mu_0(Omega_t) of trajectories that avoid H up to time t, where Omega_t={x in Omega : Phi^s(x) not in H for all s in (0,t]}, and, when it exists, the corresponding long-time escape rate gamma, what aspects of the underlying billiard dynamics can be reconstructed from those escape measurements alone? In particular, can such escape data recover, even partially, the geometry of the billiard domain D itself—that is, can one 'peep' the shape of a drum?
justification: The draft is a near-paraphrase of Problem 11.19, so the correct target is the inverse-problem question in Section 11.6, not any of the neighboring problems on local escape rates, small-hole asymptotics, or recurrence. The nearby context that makes the question mathematically stand-alone is in Section 11.3: the paper defines an open system via a hole H, the survivor set Omega_t, the survival probability P(t)=mu_0(Omega_t), and the escape rate gamma. Those definitions are the paper’s concrete meaning of 'escape measurements'. The phrase about the shape of a drum is part of the official formulation itself, with explicit bibliographic pointers in the paper to earlier work and to Kac’s classical inverse question. The paper does not state any theorem or proposition explicitly equivalent to Problem 11.19, so no alternate equivalent formulation should be added.
